audit.primary_source_citation: Whettlock EM, Woon EV, Cuff AO, Browne B, Johnson MR, Male V. "Dynamic Changes in Uterine NK Cell Subset Frequency and Function Over the Menstrual Cycle and Pregnancy." Front Immunol 2022;13:880438. PMID 35784314 / PMC9245422 / doi:10.3389/fimmu.2022.880438. UPSTREAM LABEL SOURCES (both read): Garcia-Alonso L et al., Nat Genet 2021;53:1698-1711, PMID 34857954 / PMC8648563 (source of the uNK1/2/3 names in NON-PREGNANT endometrium); Vento-Tormo R et al., Nature 2018;563:347-353, PMID 30429548 (source of the dNK1/2/3 definition in first-trimester decidua). Hint check: Wang W et al. Nat Med 2020 (PMID 32929266) EXISTS but is a misattribution for this claim - it profiles seven endometrial cell types (epithelial/stromal/ciliated) and does not define uNK1/2/3; Garcia-Alonso 2021 is the correct endometrial citation, as confirmed by fetching Whettlock's reference list (its ref 28).
audit.fulltext_unavailable_reason: Primary source full text obtained and archived (/home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC9245422.txt), as were Garcia-Alonso 2021 (S2_PMC8648563.txt), HECA/Mareckova 2024 (S2_PMC11387200.txt), Guo 2024 (S2_PMC10985329.txt) and Woon 2022 (S2_PMC9880428.txt). NOT obtainable: Vento-Tormo 2018 Nature (PMC7612850 is an EMS record that returns abstract only, so the original dNK1/2/3 clustering methods were NOT read); Strunz 2021 Sci Immunol (science.org returned HTTP 403); Strunz 2026 Sci Transl Med (abstract only); Greene 2025 bioRxiv (biorxiv 403; PMC12265685 blocked by author license). Those four were assessed from abstracts plus reference-list detail only and are flagged as such rather than paraphrased as if the methods had been read.
audit.species: Homo sapiens (human). Counter-evidence includes Mus musculus (Chiossone/Vacca 2014 adoptive transfer) and humanised mice (Strunz 2021).
audit.what_was_measured: In humans, in four separately-collected public scRNA-seq datasets spanning non-pregnant endometrium (proliferative and secretory phase) and first/second/third-trimester decidua, Seurat anchor-based integration followed by FindConservedMarkers cluster assignment was used to place cells from all stages into three shared clusters, which were then given the names uNK1/uNK2/uNK3 by reference to the pre-existing "annotation" metadata column of the first-trimester decidual dataset; in parallel, in freshly isolated ex vivo lymphocytes, flow-cytometric frequency of CD49a+ CD39/CD103 gates (uNK1 = CD39+CD103-, uNK2 = CD39-CD103-, uNK3 = CD103+), surface KIR2DL1/S1, KIR2DL2/3, LILRB1 and CD94, and CD107a degranulation plus intracellular TNFa/IFNg/IL-8/GM-CSF after 4-6 h PMA+ionomycin, were measured at seven cross-sectional reproductive-cycle stages. NO cell was tracked from endometrium into decidua: no donor contributed both a non-pregnant and a pregnant sample, and no lineage label (barcode, allele, dye, transfer) linked any endometrial cell to any decidual cell. Timepoints are donor cohorts, not repeated measures on the same tissue.
audit.n: scRNA-seq arm (the arm that actually carries the endometrium-to-decidua correspondence): 6 non-pregnant endometrium donors (3 proliferative + 3 secretory, reanalysed from Garcia-Alonso 2021) vs 5 first-trimester decidua donors (E-MTAB-6701, after 1 donor was discarded for clustering independently), plus 1 second-trimester (a pathological accreta case) and 3 third-trimester donors. Flow arm (new data): 29 endometrial biopsies (8 menstrual, 7 proliferative, 10 secretory), 4 postpartum, 10 first-trimester decidua, 16 third-trimester elective caesarean, plus 9 early-labour and 9 vaginal-birth samples; matched peripheral blood from all. Overlap between non-pregnant and pregnant groups = 0 donors. Upstream sources: Garcia-Alonso 2021 = 3 live-donor biopsies + 6 deceased-donor whole uteri.
audit.n_unit: donors (individual women); NOT cells. Cell counts (2,180 endometrial, 18,243 first-trimester, 3,900 second-trimester, 6,077 third-trimester) are pseudoreplicates within these donors.
audit.controls: Present: matched peripheral blood CD56bright/CD56dim NK from every donor (used to show pNK frequency and receptor expression do NOT vary across the cycle, so the uNK changes are not a blood artefact); CD49a (+/-CD9) tissue-residency gating to exclude contaminating pNK, with an explicit check that CD49a+CD9- and CD49a+CD9+ term cells are phenotypically identical; paired unstimulated vs PMA/ionomycin wells; fresh-vs-rested stimulation optimisation; exclusion of placental and blood cells from the decidual objects; removal of one aberrant first-trimester donor; equal-cell downsampling per dataset for visualisation. ABSENT and decisive: (i) no paired/longitudinal donor sampled both before and during pregnancy; (ii) no negative control for the integration procedure - no test that anchor-based integration of two unrelated tissues fails to produce three matched clusters when no lineage relationship exists; (iii) no clustering-resolution stability analysis; (iv) no donor-genotype or any other cell-intrinsic label capable of distinguishing a carried-over cell from a newly recruited one. The authors' own third-trimester result is an internal control that failed in the direction of artefact: term decidual uNK formed only ONE cluster when analysed alone and split into three only after integration with the other datasets.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: The correspondence is circular by construction, not observed. The endometrial subsets were never independently named: Garcia-Alonso 2021, the paper Whettlock cites for "uNK1/2/3 are present in non-pregnant endometrium", states that subclustering of endometrial immune cells identified "the three uterine natural killer cell subsets WE HAVE PREVIOUSLY DEFINED IN THE EARLY PREGNANT UTERUS", annotated "by manual inspection of marker genes and interpretation of these based on the literature"; Whettlock then assigned labels with FindConservedMarkers "confirmed by the metadata column 'annotation' from the first-trimester dataset"; and the HECA reference atlas (Mareckova 2024) projected the same labels with a CellTypist logistic-regression classifier trained on that reference. A decidual reference was therefore used to name the endometrial cells, so recovering a 1:1 endometrium-decidua match is guaranteed whether or not any endometrial cell ever becomes a decidual cell. The concrete non-carriage model that fits all the same data: uNK are re-recruited from circulating precursors after each menses and the three states are re-generated in situ by differential TGF-beta/IL-15 exposure, so endometrium and decidua contain independently generated instances of the same three attractor states rather than the same cells carried forward (Greene 2025; Strunz 2021). A second, purely technical alternative: the "three subsets" is a clustering-resolution choice, not an entity - Guo 2024, using identically processed endometrium and decidua, resolves NK1a/NK1b/NK2a/NK2b/NK3 plus three proliferating NK clusters at higher resolution, and Whettlock's own term-decidua uNK collapse to a single cluster unless integrated with the other tissues. Note for the record: no pseudotime or RNA-velocity was run on the NK compartment in the primary source, so this is not an INF_TRAJECTORY case - it is weaker still, being static cross-cohort label matching.
audit.counter_evidence: (1) Strunz B et al., "Reconstitution of the uterine immune milieu after uterus or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation", Sci Transl Med 2026;18:eadp2583, PMID 41811987 - human uterus transplant and HSCT recipients; donor-vs-recipient origin of endometrial immune cells resolved GENETICALLY by SNP-based demultiplexing of scRNA-seq and by disparate HLA expression on flow: "Recipient-derived immune cells replaced donor immune cells after uterus transplant, whereas HSCT resulted in near-complete donor-derived immune reconstitution, including formation of tissue-resident lymphocytes", with one patient's endometrium reconstituted by male-origin cells. The endometrial uNK pool is therefore continuously replaced from circulation and is not a persistent compartment that can be carried anywhere. (2) Strunz B et al., Sci Immunol 2021;6:eabb7800, PMID 33617461 - surface proteome/transcriptome plus humanised mice, human uterus transplantation and monozygotic twins; reports CONTINUOUS uNK differentiation with sequential KIR then CD39 acquisition driven by IL-15, and that "the uNK cell niche could be replenished from circulation". A continuum with sequential marker acquisition is incompatible with three discrete pre-formed subsets being carried across tissues (abstract only; science.org 403). (3) Greene M, ... Porrett PM, bioRxiv 2025.07.05.663267, PMID 40672293 - "uNKs derive from circulatory cells in the peripheral blood which immigrate into the endometrium and become resident as they reconstitute the uterine lining after menses"; divergent effector uNK subsets are produced by differences in TGF-beta responsiveness of recent immigrants, i.e. subsets are made in situ each cycle, not inherited (full text unobtainable). (4) Chiossone L, Vacca P et al., Haematologica 2014;99:448-457, PMID 24179150 - EGFP+ adoptive transfer in pregnant mice: mature peripheral NK did NOT migrate into decidua/uterus, whereas NK precursors were recruited and differentiated in situ. Direct transfer evidence for de novo generation of decidual NK (mouse; cross-species caveat). (5) Guo/Penn, Front Immunol 2024;15:1364036, PMID 38566989 - identically processed mid-secretory endometrium (n=4) and first-trimester decidua (n=4), Seurat-integrated: subsets split into NK1a/NK1b/NK2a/NK2b/NK3 plus three proliferating clusters, composition and gene expression change pre- to post-implantation, and the authors note the proliferating clusters "may represent precursor populations that give rise to particular types of NK cells". Nothing found supporting carriage: I searched specifically for paired/longitudinal same-donor endometrium-to-decidua designs and for any lineage-label or chimerism test of carriage and found none.
audit.downstream_dependency: NAMED DEPENDENCY 1: Woon EV, Greer O, Shah N, Male V, Johnson MR et al., "Uterine NK cells underexpress KIR2DL1/S1 and LILRB1 in reproductive failure", Front Immunol 2022;13:1108163, PMID 36713400 / PMC9880428. It gates uNK1-3 in NON-PREGNANT window-of-implantation endometrium from 16 women with unexplained reproductive failure vs 11 controls and concludes that reproductive failure involves "reduction in expression of uNK receptors important for interaction with HLA-C and HLA-G on EVT DURING EARLY PREGNANCY". That inference is only valid if the endometrial uNK1/2/3 measured pre-conception are the cells that will be the decidual dNK1/2/3 facing extravillous trophoblast. If instead the uNK pool is re-recruited and re-differentiated after implantation, a pre-conception biopsy cannot index decidual subset composition and the entire pre-conception "uNK subset test" rationale for recurrent miscarriage / recurrent implantation failure clinics loses its bridge. NAMED DEPENDENCY 2: Mareckova M, Garcia-Alonso L, Vento-Tormo R et al., "An integrated single-cell reference atlas of the human endometrium" (HECA), Nat Genet 2024;56:1925-1937, PMID 39198675 - hard-codes uNK1/2/3 as consensus non-pregnant endometrial cell-state labels (assigned by CellTypist logistic-regression label projection, then marker-refined) into the community reference atlas that is subsequently integrated with endometriosis GWAS data; every downstream study that maps a query dataset onto HECA inherits the decidua-derived subset identity without re-testing it. NAMED DEPENDENCY 3: the primary source's own stated purpose - Whettlock 2022 positions its cross-sectional cycle data as "a platform from which the relationship between uNK function and impaired implantation and placentation can be investigated".
audit.audit_overturns_detail: The CLASS is not overturned: Claude called it INFERENCE (shared markers) and the audit confirms INF_MARKER as the strongest class. Three substantive corrections make the claim materially weaker than that label suggests. (a) It is not an independent marker match, it is CIRCULAR. Claude's phrasing implies two separately derived label sets that happened to agree. In fact the endometrial labels were created by importing the decidual ones - Garcia-Alonso 2021 says the endometrial subsets are "the three uterine natural killer cell subsets we have previously defined in the early pregnant uterus"; Whettlock's assignment was "confirmed by the metadata column 'annotation' from the first-trimester dataset"; HECA projected the labels with a CellTypist classifier. Agreement is an artefact of the naming pipeline, so this sits at the very bottom of INF_MARKER, not the middle. (b) The claim is not merely unsupported but AFFIRMATIVELY CONTRADICTED by evidence of a stronger class than the claim itself rests on: OBS_GENETIC chimerism in human uterus transplant/HSCT (Strunz 2026) showing the endometrial immune compartment including tissue-resident lymphocytes is replaced from circulation, and OBS_TRANSFER in mouse (Chiossone 2014) showing mature NK do not enter decidua while precursors do. Claude's call did not register that counter-evidence exists. (c) The three-subset partition is resolution-dependent, not an entity: Whettlock's own term decidua yields ONE uNK cluster alone and three only after integration with the other tissues, and Guo 2024 resolves five effector plus three proliferating clusters from the same tissues. Also corrected: the starting hint's "Wang et al. Nat Med 2020" is a misattribution for the endometrial uNK subsets (that paper exists, PMID 32929266, but describes seven epithelial/stromal cell types and no uNK1/2/3); the correct endometrial citation is Garcia-Alonso Nat Genet 2021, verified from Whettlock's reference list. One point in Claude's favour that I checked and can confirm: this is NOT a pseudotime claim - no trajectory or velocity was run on the NK compartment in any of the load-bearing papers.
audit.methods_quote: Whettlock 2022, Methods, "Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Data Analysis": "The four datasets were integrated based on a previously published workflow. Clusters that appeared to be non-immune cells were removed, and the remaining cells were reanalysed using the same workflow. The integrated dataset contained 2,180 cells from non-pregnant endometrium, 18,243 cells from first-trimester decidua, 3,900 from second-trimester decidua, and 6,077 from third-trimester decidua. The algorithm 'FindConservedMarkers' was used to identify the clusters uNK1, uNK2, and uNK3. This was confirmed by the metadata column 'annotation' from the first-trimester dataset." || Whettlock 2022, Results: "Previous analysis of scRNAseq data from third-trimester decidua identified only a single cluster within the uNK population, and our reanalysis of the third-trimester dataset alone confirmed this. However, when the third-trimester data were integrated with data from the non-pregnant uterus, first- and second-trimester, the third-trimester uNK cells did form three clusters." || Garcia-Alonso 2021 (PMID 34857954), Results: "Subclustering of immune cells resolves their heterogeneity, including identification of the three uterine natural killer cell subsets we have previously defined in the early pregnant uterus"; Methods, "Annotation of scRNA-seq datasets": "Identification and labeling of the major cell types in the in vivo dataset was by manual inspection of marker genes and interpretation of these based on the literature." || Mareckova 2024 HECA (PMID 39198675), Methods: "To annotate immune cells in our datasets we first used celltypist v.0.1.9, which is a logistic regression classifier optimized by the stochastic gradient descent algorithm... After projecting labels from all three datasets, we refined the annotations using expression of bona fide markers on each cluster."
audit.notes: VERDICT: the "same subsets carried from endometrium into decidua" reading of S2 is not supported by any observation in any located primary source, and is contradicted by human transplant-chimerism and mouse transfer data. What IS supported is the much weaker statement: three transcriptionally/phenotypically analogous uNK states are detectable in both non-pregnant endometrium and decidua, in separate cross-sectional donor cohorts, with the endometrial states named after the decidual ones. The arrow in "uNK1/2/3 -> dNK1/2/3" is supplied by the reader, not by data. || Archived full texts: /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC9245422.txt (Whettlock 2022, primary), /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC8648563.txt (Garcia-Alonso 2021), /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC11387200.txt (HECA 2024), /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC10985329.txt (Guo 2024), /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC9880428.txt (Woon 2022), /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC7612850.txt (Vento-Tormo 2018, abstract only), /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_33617461.txt and S2_41811987.txt and S2_40672293.txt (abstract only), /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC3943307.txt (Chiossone 2014, abstract only). || G5 compliance: every n above is donors/women; the 2,180 / 18,243 / 3,900 / 6,077 figures are cells and are recorded only as pseudoreplicate counts. || in_vivo field set to in_vivo because the load-bearing evidence is profiling of freshly isolated ex vivo tissue; the PMA/ionomycin degranulation and cytokine assays are in vitro readouts on ex vivo cells and bear on function, not on the lineage claim, so INF_INVITRO is not listed. || Uncertainty flagged honestly: Vento-Tormo 2018's original clustering methods for dNK1/2/3 could not be read (PMC record is abstract-only), so the claim that dNK1/2/3 themselves are Leiden clusters plus marker annotation is inferred from the abstract, from Whettlock's use of its "annotation" metadata column, and from Garcia-Alonso's description of them - not read from that paper's methods.

adv.challenge_reason: I re-pulled the primary source methods myself (python3 scripts/lit.py methods 35784314 --tag S2ADV -> STATUS=OA_FULLTEXT PMID=35784314 PMCID=PMC9245422, archived /home/user/aaa/refs/S2ADV_PMC9245422.txt) and read "Primary Tissue", "Stimulation With PMA/Ionomycin", "Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Data Analysis", "Flow Cytometry" and "Statistical Analysis" verbatim rather than the abstract. The auditor did NOT credit an OBS_* class to marker similarity, and did NOT miss a fate-mapping/congenic/barcoding experiment inside the primary source. Verified in the methods text: (i) the endometrium-to-decidua correspondence rests entirely on Seurat anchor integration of FOUR SEPARATELY COLLECTED PUBLIC DATASETS (reproductivecellatlas.org non-pregnant; E-MTAB-6701 first trimester; dbGaP phs001886.v1.p1 second/third trimester) followed by "FindConservedMarkers ... to identify the clusters uNK1, uNK2, and uNK3. This was confirmed by the metadata column 'annotation' from the first-trimester dataset" - i.e. cluster-label matching, INF_MARKER; (ii) I grepped all archived load-bearing texts for pseudotime|velocity|monocle|slingshot|trajector|PAGA - the ONLY hit in Whettlock is zero, and the only hit in Garcia-Alonso 2021 (PMC8648563) is trajectory analysis of EPITHELIAL ORGANOID data, not the NK compartment. So G2 does not bite and the auditor's note that this is not an INF_TRAJECTORY case is confirmed by me independently; (iii) no barcode, dye, congenic marker, donor genotype, SNP demultiplex or transfer appears anywhere in the methods; (iv) the PMA/ionomycin arm (4 h endometrium/first trimester, 6 h third trimester) is a function readout on ex vivo cells and carries no lineage information, so excluding INF_INVITRO from the primary source was correct. INF_KINETIC is correctly listed as present but I would sharpen it: it is CROSS-COHORT, not longitudinal - seven reproductive stages sampled in disjoint donor groups, never repeated measures. THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE ROW. (1) n arithmetic error, G5-relevant: the row states "29 endometrial biopsies (8 menstrual, 7 proliferative, 10 secretory), 4 postpartum", implying 33. The methods read "A total of 29 endometrial samples ... We collected 8 menstrual, 7 proliferative, and 10 secretory phase samples AND 4 samples from postpartum participants" - 8+7+10+4=29, so the 4 postpartum are INSIDE the 29, and the cycling-endometrium flow n is 25 women, not 29. (2) A technical-artefact confound the auditor missed entirely: the three tissue types were dissociated by DIFFERENT protocols in the same paper - endometrium by 100 um then 70 um strainer with no enzyme; first-trimester decidua by gentleMACS, no enzyme; third-trimester decidua by ACCUTASE plus gentleMACS in a 37 C shaking water bath for 45 MIN. The subsets are defined by two protease/ectoenzyme-sensitive surface markers (CD39, CD103) on CD49a+ cells, so cross-stage subset-frequency comparison - the paper's central kinetic result - is confounded by protocol-dependent epitope stripping and differential recovery, independently of any lineage question. (3) SCOPE-DEPENDENCE THAT THE ROW DOES NOT STATE, and the only reason I stop short of UPGRADE: for S2 AS WRITTEN ("the same subsets uNK1/2/3 carried into dNK1/2/3") INF_MARKER is right and I uphold it. But if the claim is read at the bulk compartment level ("endometrial uNK become decidual uNK"), the located evidence base contains classes the auditor never surfaced - INF_INVITRO in Manaster I et al., J Immunol 2008;181:1869-76, PMID 18641324, which shows eNK are functionally inert until IL-15 and then "acquire phenotype and function that are similar to those of decidual NK cells", and mouse OBS_TRANSFER in Sojka DK et al., J Immunol 2018;201:2551-6, PMID 30275046 (see counter-evidence field). Per G7 I do not loosen the class to capture that: mouse has no uNK1/2/3 partition and Manaster predates the subsets by a decade, so neither speaks to subset identity. Strongest class for S2 as stated remains INF_MARKER, and the auditor's characterisation of it as CIRCULAR INF_MARKER (endometrial labels imported from the decidual reference) is one I independently verified in Garcia-Alonso 2021 line 28: "Subclustering of immune cells resolves their heterogeneity, including identification of the three uterine natural killer cell subsets we have previously defined in the early pregnant uterus." I also independently verified the row's Wang-2020 misattribution finding: /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_32929266.txt contains zero occurrences of uNK/NK-subset annotation and profiles "seven endometrial cell types" - the row is right that PMID 32929266 exists but is the wrong citation.
adv.revised_evidence_type_strongest: INF_MARKER (unchanged). evidence_types_all revised to: INF_MARKER (primary, and circular - endometrial labels derived from the decidual reference), INF_KINETIC (present but cross-cohort, not longitudinal; and confounded by three different tissue-dissociation protocols acting on the protease-sensitive CD39/CD103 markers that define the subsets). Not present in the primary source: OBS_DIRECT, OBS_TRANSFER, OBS_GENETIC, INF_INVITRO, INF_TRAJECTORY. Scope note per G7: at the bulk compartment level the wider located literature would add INF_INVITRO (PMID 18641324, PMID 17360654) and mouse OBS_TRANSFER (PMID 30275046, PMID 39708955, PMID 24179150), but none of these resolves the three named subsets, so the class for S2 as written is not upgraded.
adv.new_counter_evidence: FIVE items the auditor did not have, three of which change the row's balance. (1) MOST IMPORTANT - THE "PRE-EXISTING SUBSET IS EXPANDED, NOT CONVERTED" TEST EXISTS AND THE AUDITOR MISSED IT, AND IT CUTS THE OTHER WAY: Sojka DK, Yang L, Plougastel-Douglas B, Higuchi DA, Croy BA, Yokoyama WM. "Cutting Edge: Local Proliferation of Uterine Tissue-Resident NK Cells during Decidualization in Mice." J Immunol 2018;201:2551-2556, PMID 30275046 / PMC6552671. Mouse, in vivo, NK-specific reporter mouse plus PARABIOSIS with experimentally induced deciduomata: "Only trNK cells showed evidence of proliferation. In parabiosis studies using experimentally induced deciduomata, the accumulated uNK cells were proliferating trNK cells; MIGRATING NK CELLS MADE NO CONTRIBUTION. Together, these data suggest proliferating trNK cells are the source of uNK cells during endometrial decidualization." This is OBS_TRANSFER-grade evidence FOR compartment-level carriage - the pre-pregnancy uterine trNK pool expands in place to become the decidual pool - and it DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS the auditor's item (4), Chiossone/Vacca 2014 (PMID 24179150), which the row presented as unopposed transfer evidence that dNK are made de novo from recruited precursors. Two mouse studies of the same class disagree; the row reported only the one that suited its verdict. Note precisely what Sojka 2018 does and does not license: it supports carriage of a POOL, not of three named subsets (mouse uNK are partitioned trNK vs cNK, there is no uNK1/2/3), so it does not rescue S2 as written - but the row's flat statement that carriage is "contradicted by mouse transfer data" is one-sided and must be corrected. (2) SAME LAB, REVERSED CONCLUSION - Tatematsu BK, Sojka DK. "Tissue-resident natural killer cells derived from conventional natural killer cells are regulated by progesterone in the uterus." Mucosal Immunol 2025;18:390-401, PMID 39708955. Mouse, PARABIOSIS plus intravascular antibody labelling plus ovariectomy/hormone add-back: mice ovariectomised at 3 weeks "lacked uterine trNK cells unless progesterone was administered", and "Our parabiosis studies confirmed that the progesterone-responsive trNK cells are DERIVED FROM PERIPHERAL cNK CELLS." So the uterine trNK compartment is itself continuously generated from circulating cNK under progesterone control - i.e. the pool that Sojka 2018 shows expanding locally is itself hormonally re-derived, and its size and composition are set by the current hormonal state, not inherited. Together (1)+(2) are the mouse field arguing with itself using the correct methodology, and neither supports subset carriage. (3) INDEPENDENT HUMAN EVIDENCE OF RAPID LOCAL TURNOVER OF ENDOMETRIAL NK - Feyaerts D, Kuret T, van Cranenbroek B, van der Zeeuw-Hingrez S, van der Heijden OWH, van der Meer A, Joosten I, van der Molen RG. "Endometrial natural killer (NK) cells reveal a tissue-specific receptor repertoire." Hum Reprod 2018;33:441-451, PMID 29447367. n=25 healthy women, matched menstrual-cup-derived endometrial NK and peripheral blood NK, 10-colour flow, KIR/HLA-C genotyped by PCR-SSOP, sampled over CONSECUTIVE CYCLES: "the typical NKG2C imprint induced by CMV infection on pbNK cells was NOT observed on eNK cells from the same female, SUGGESTING A RAPID LOCAL TURNOVER OF eNK CELLS and/or a distinct licensing process." A cell-intrinsic, historically-imprinted marker (CMV-driven NKG2C expansion) present in the same woman's blood but absent from her endometrium is the closest thing in the human literature to a negative lineage-persistence test, and it argues against a long-lived carried endometrial pool. This is the within-donor longitudinal human design the row asserted did not exist - it exists for the cycle, though still not across the endometrium-to-pregnancy transition. (4) COUNTER-COUNTER-EVIDENCE THE ROW ALSO MISSED, which I record for fairness because it is the strongest published argument on the carriage side - Ivarsson MA, Stiglund N, Marquardt N, Westgren M, Gidlof S, Bjorkstrom NK. "Composition and dynamics of the uterine NK cell KIR repertoire in menstrual blood." Mucosal Immunol 2017;10:322-331, PMID 27271316. Paired menstrual and peripheral blood, six inhibitory/activating KIRs: uterine NK KIR repertoires are strongly KIR2D-biased, HLA-independent, contain NKG2C+self-KIR+ expansions, and "the distinct KIR repertoires of uterine NK cells were STABLE OVER MULTIPLE MENSTRUAL CYCLES." Repertoire stability across cycles is consistent with a persisting pool - but it is a population-composition measure, not a lineage label, and would be reproduced identically by a niche that re-imposes the same bias on newly recruited cells each cycle (which is exactly what Tatematsu/Sojka 2025 shows the uterus doing under progesterone). So it remains INF_MARKER-grade and does not lift S2. (5) A 2026 HUMAN UTERUS-TRANSPLANT PAPER THAT THE ROW FETCHED BUT NEVER USED - Asiimwe R, Knott B, Greene ME, ... Freud AG, Little SC, Porrett PM. "Inhibition of NFAT after human uterus transplant promotes loss of tissue-resident NK cells and attendant pregnancy complications." Sci Transl Med 2026;18:eadp2196, PMID 41811989 / PMC13095030 (archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC13095030.txt - present in the refs directory but absent from the row's counter_evidence, and only listed in searches_run). Human UTx recipients vs healthy controls, flow + immunofluorescence + scRNA-seq of endometrial biopsies AND deciduae: tissue-resident uNK subsets are REDUCED in both compartments under tacrolimus, "the NK cell reduction ... correlated with impaired transcriptional programming of NK TISSUE RESIDENCY", with residency described as a staged programme (early AP-1-dependent, later TGF-beta-driven integrin upregulation). If residency must be actively and continuously programmed in situ, and a calcineurin inhibitor can abolish it in an adult uterus, the compartment is a maintained steady state, not a heirloom. Also note this paper reports uNK subset deficiency causing preeclampsia in the SAME transplanted uterus that later carries a pregnancy - the nearest existing approximation to a within-organ endometrium-to-decidua design, and it still carries no cell-intrinsic label. Additional item confirming the row's alternative model: Vacca P, Vitale C, Montaldo E, Conte R, Cantoni C, Fulcheri E, Darretta V, Moretta L, Mingari MC. NOT SEARCHED / NOT FOUND, recorded honestly: I did not find, and did not locate any search that would find, a human study using a cell-intrinsic lineage label (mtDNA variant, SNP demultiplexing, X-inactivation, chimerism, barcode) applied to the SAME woman's endometrium and subsequent decidua. adv.crossfield_g4_findings: I searched the TRM/T cell, ILC and myeloid literatures on the structural question S2 actually turns on - "does recovering the same marker-defined subsets at two timepoints in a tissue mean the cells were carried?" - not the NK literature. Four things those fields establish, all of which bear against S2 and none of which the auditor invoked. (A) THE MYELOID FIELD SETTLED THIS EXACT QUESTION AND THE ANSWER IS NO. van de Laar L, Saelens W, De Prijck S, Martens L, Scott CL, et al. "Yolk Sac Macrophages, Fetal Liver, and Adult Monocytes Can Colonize an Empty Niche and Develop into Functional Tissue-Resident Macrophages." Immunity 2016;44:755-768, PMID 26992565. Traceable yolk-sac macrophages, fetal-liver monocytes and adult bone-marrow monocytes were transferred separately into the empty alveolar niche of neonatal Csf2rb-/- mice: "all precursors efficiently colonized the alveolar niche and generated AMs that were TRANSCRIPTIONALLY ALMOST IDENTICAL, self-maintained, and durably prevented alveolar proteinosis. Thus, PRECURSOR ORIGIN DOES NOT AFFECT the development of functional self-maintaining tissue-resident macrophages." This is a competitive, fate-mapped, in vivo demonstration that a tissue niche imposes a transcriptional identity on whatever enters it. Applied to S2: recovering three transcriptionally matched uNK states in decidua is exactly what the non-carriage model predicts, so the observation has essentially no discriminating power. The complementary result - Ginhoux F et al., Science 2010;330:841-5, PMID 20966214, and Hashimoto D et al., Immunity 2013;38:792-804, PMID 23601688 - is that cells sharing an identical marker phenotype in one tissue can have entirely distinct ontogenies, only resolvable by fate mapping. Marker identity is neither necessary nor sufficient for lineage continuity. (B) THE TRM FIELD SUPPLIES THE METHODOLOGY THE UTERINE FIELD HAS NOT APPLIED WITHIN A DONOR, AND SHOWS DE NOVO SUBSET REGENERATION. Snyder ME, Finlayson MO, Connors TJ, et al. "Generation and persistence of human tissue-resident memory T cells in lung transplantation." Sci Immunol 2019;4:eaav5581, PMID 30850393 - longitudinal airway sampling in HLA-DISPARATE lung transplant recipients, donor and recipient cells tracked by HLA: donor T cells persist in lung and express CD69/CD103/CD49a, while "lung-infiltrating RECIPIENT T cells GRADUALLY ACQUIRE TRM PHENOTYPES OVER MONTHS in vivo", and scRNA-seq showed recipient cells forming "similar TRM-like subpopulations, SUGGESTING DE NOVO TRM GENERATION". That is the precise structural counterexample: two cell pools of entirely different origin converge on the same marker-defined subsets in the same tissue. Bartolome-Casado R et al., J Exp Med 2019;216:2412-2426, PMID 31337737, shows the opposite outcome is also possible (donor CD8 TRM persist for years in transplanted human duodenum) - which is the point: persistence versus replacement is TISSUE-SPECIFIC and can only be settled by a chimerism or parabiosis experiment, never by phenotype. The uterus is the tissue where the chimerism experiment has been run (Strunz 2026 PMID 41811987; Asiimwe/Porrett 2026 PMID 41811989) and it came out on the replacement side. (C) THE T CELL FIELD HAS AN EXPLICIT FORMAL CRITIQUE OF MARKER-DEFINED SUBSETS STANDING IN FOR BEHAVIOURAL CLAIMS, AND IT ALSO INDICTS THE FREQUENCY COMPARISON. Steinert EM, Schenkel JM, et al. "Quantifying Memory CD8 T Cells Reveals Regionalization of Immunosurveillance." Cell 2015;161:737-749, PMID 25957682: "Paradigmatically, memory is parsed into central, effector, and resident subsets, OSTENSIBLY DEFINED BY IMMUNOSURVEILLANCE PATTERNS BUT IN PRACTICE IDENTIFIED BY PHENOTYPIC MARKERS ... we tested their validity via parabiosis and quantitative immunofluorescence microscopy" and found "lymphocyte isolation FAILS TO RECOVER MOST CELLS AND BIASES AGAINST CERTAIN SUBSETS". This is the same failure mode as S2 at two levels: a subset named for a fate but identified by CD39/CD103, and a cross-tissue frequency comparison built on isolation yields - which in Whettlock come from three DIFFERENT dissociation protocols (no enzyme for endometrium, gentleMACS for first trimester, 45 min Accutase at 37 C for third trimester). Steinert is the formal reason that comparison cannot be read as a subset-frequency time course. (D) THE ILC FIELD SHOWS TISSUE, NOT LINEAGE, DOMINATES THE TRANSCRIPTOME AND THAT SUBSET COUNT IS A RESOLUTION CHOICE. Mazzurana L, Czarnewski P, ... Mjosberg J. "Tissue-specific transcriptional imprinting and heterogeneity in human innate lymphoid cells revealed by full-length single-cell RNA-sequencing." Cell Res 2021;31:554-568, PMID 33420427 / PMC8089104 (full text archived, /home/user/aaa/refs/S2G4_PMC8089104.txt) - across multiple human tissues the tissue of residence imprints ILC transcriptomes more strongly than canonical subset identity, and Bjorklund AK et al., Nat Immunol 2016;17:451-460, PMID 26878113 showed human CD127+ ILC "subsets" resolve as graded heterogeneity by scRNA-seq. Both undercut the premise that "three subsets" is a transferable entity rather than a partition of a continuum - which is precisely the Guo 2024 (PMID 38566989, five effector + three proliferating clusters) and term-decidua-collapses-to-one-cluster problem the auditor identified from within the NK data. NET G4 VERDICT: every field that has run the decisive experiment (myeloid fate mapping, TRM parabiosis and transplant chimerism, ILC cross-tissue scRNA-seq) concludes that marker-defined or transcriptome-defined subset correspondence across two timepoints or two tissues carries no lineage information, and that niche instruction reliably regenerates the same states from unrelated precursors. S2's entire evidentiary basis is the kind of observation those fields specifically established to be uninformative.

adv.load_bearing_reason: HIGH is upheld, and I can name a dependency stronger and more current than the three the row listed. I verified the row's Dependency 1 by reading the archived text: Woon EV et al., Front Immunol 2022;13:1108163, PMID 36713400 / PMC9880428 (/home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC9880428.txt) gates uNK1/2/3 by CD49a/CD39/CD103 in MID-LUTEAL, NON-PREGNANT endometrium from 16 women with unexplained reproductive failure vs 11 controls and concludes that "reproductive failure is associated with global reduction in expression of uNK receptors important for interaction with HLA-C and HLA-G on EVT DURING EARLY PREGNANCY, leading to reduced uNK activation", explicitly positioning itself as the pre-conception alternative to post-miscarriage decidual sampling ("these studies were performed in decidua collected after miscarriage ... Therefore, the question remains, how do uNK subsets behave in the ENDOMETRIUM of women with reproductive failure?"). That inference is valid only if the pre-conception endometrial uNK1/2/3 measured in a coil-fitting clinic are the cells that will face extravillous trophoblast as dNK1/2/3. It is a clinical-test rationale resting directly on S2. THE STRONGER, NEWER DEPENDENCY THE ROW HAD IN ITS REFS DIRECTORY BUT DID NOT USE: Asiimwe R, Knott B, Greene ME, ... Freud AG, Little SC, Porrett PM, "Inhibition of NFAT after human uterus transplant promotes loss of tissue-resident NK cells and attendant pregnancy complications", Sci Transl Med 2026;18:eadp2196, PMID 41811989 / PMC13095030 (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/S2_PMC13095030.txt). It pools "subsets of tissue-resident uNK cells ... in ENDOMETRIAL AND DECIDUAL SAMPLES" from uterus-transplant recipients as one continuous entity, and uses a deficit measured in that pooled entity to explain maternal vascular malperfusion and preeclampsia - a 2026 clinical causal claim about transplant management (tacrolimus/NFAT inhibition) whose logic requires that endometrial and decidual uNK subsets be the same population at two timepoints. If the decidual pool is re-recruited and re-differentiated post-implantation under progesterone and TGF-beta (which that paper's own staged residency programme and Tatematsu/Sojka 2025 PMID 39708955 both suggest), an endometrial biopsy measured under tacrolimus does not index the decidual state, and the drug-to-preeclampsia bridge needs re-deriving. That is a named, dated, patient-facing dependency, which is why I do not downgrade. Two further dependencies stand as the row stated them: Mareckova M, Garcia-Alonso L, ... Vento-Tormo R, HECA, Nat Genet 2024;56:1925-1937, PMID 39198675, hard-codes uNK1/2/3 as consensus non-pregnant endometrial cell states assigned by CellTypist logistic-regression label projection, so every dataset later mapped onto HECA silently inherits the decidua-derived subset identity; and Whettlock 2022's own closing sentence positions the work as "an important platform from which the relationship between uNK function and pathologies of pregnancy associated with impaired implantation and placentation can be investigated". The only argument for downgrade I considered and rejected: one could say the clinical work needs merely a PREDICTIVE bridge (pre-conception composition correlates with decidual composition) rather than literal cell carriage. But that predictive bridge has never been tested in any located study, and it is exactly what the counter-evidence attacks - Feyaerts 2018 (PMID 29447367) reports rapid local eNK turnover, Tatematsu/Sojka 2025 shows the uterine trNK pool is progesterone-dependent and cNK-derived, and pregnancy imposes a hormonal state utterly unlike the mid-luteal biopsy. So the weaker reading is no safer than the strong one, and load-bearing stays HIGH.
adv.better_primary_source: NO better primary source for S2 as written. I re-checked the alternatives and Whettlock 2022 (PMID 35784314 / PMC9245422) remains the only located human study that puts non-pregnant endometrium and all three trimesters of decidua into one analysis, so it is correctly identified. The row's upstream attribution is also correct and I verified it independently: Garcia-Alonso 2021 (PMID 34857954 / PMC8648563) is the source of the uNK1/2/3 names in non-pregnant endometrium - line 28, "identification of the three uterine natural killer cell subsets we have previously defined in the early pregnant uterus" - and Wang 2020 Nat Med (PMID 32929266) is a genuine misattribution, confirmed by grepping the archived record (/home/user/aaa/refs/S2_32929266.txt), which describes seven epithelial/stromal/ciliated cell types and contains no uNK subset annotation. THE ROW'S REAL SOURCING DEFECT IS NOT THE PRIMARY SOURCE, IT IS THE MECHANISM SOURCES, WHICH ARE MISSING. The claim is a recruitment-versus-residency claim, and the primary sources for THAT are all absent from the row: Sojka DK et al., J Immunol 2018;201:2551-2556, PMID 30275046 / PMC6552671 (mouse, parabiosis + NK reporter, uNK during decidualization are locally proliferating pre-existing trNK with no contribution from migrating cells - the strongest evidence FOR compartment-level carriage in any species, and it contradicts the row's Chiossone 2014 item); Tatematsu BK & Sojka DK, Mucosal Immunol 2025;18:390-401, PMID 39708955 (mouse, parabiosis + intravascular labelling + ovariectomy, uterine trNK derive from peripheral cNK and require progesterone); Asiimwe R ... Porrett PM, Sci Transl Med 2026;18:eadp2196, PMID 41811989 / PMC13095030 (human uterus transplant, endometrium AND decidua, staged NFAT-dependent residency programming); Feyaerts D et al., Hum Reprod 2018;33:441-451, PMID 29447367 (human, n=25, consecutive cycles, absent CMV/NKG2C imprint on eNK implies rapid local turnover); Ivarsson MA et al., Mucosal Immunol 2017;10:322-331, PMID 27271316 (human, uNK KIR repertoire stable over multiple cycles - the best counter-counter item, still INF_MARKER); Manaster I et al., J Immunol 2008;181:1869-1876, PMID 18641324 (human, IL-15 converts inert eNK to a dNK-like phenotype - INF_INVITRO support for a bulk-level version of the claim, entirely absent from the row); and Vacca P et al., PNAS 2011;108:2402-2407, PMID 21248224 (human, CD34+ precursors resident in decidua differentiate to NK on decidual-stromal coculture). One further item worth adding to the row's alternative-explanation field: Derivation of functional early gestation decidual natural killer cell subtypes from induced pluripotent stem cells, bioRxiv 2025, PMID 41279445 / PMC12637421 (OA full text obtained, archived /home/user/aaa/refs/S2ADV_PMC12637421.txt) - if dNK subtypes can be generated from iPSC with no endometrium anywhere in the system, the three states are a reachable differentiation attractor rather than an inherited identity, which is the cleanest available statement of the non-carriage model. FINALLY, THE EXPERIMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE S2 AND HAS NOT BEEN DONE: no located study applies a cell-intrinsic retrospective lineage label - mitochondrial DNA variant tracing (the method exists and is validated in human tissue, e.g. PMID 38253266, PMID 40134031), SNP demultiplexing, or X-inactivation mosaicism - to the same woman's endometrium and her subsequent decidua. Until that is done, the arrow in "uNK1/2/3 -> dNK1/2/3" is supplied by the naming pipeline, and I concur with the prior row's verdict on that point even while correcting its one-sided reading of the mouse transfer literature.
